# Modules

Every shared file, what it is for (its own header comment) and what it exports.

## `src/lib/acting.ts`

"View as": an admin can use the field app as a merchandiser or a marketer,
to test-run clock-in, store visits and reports in different places. The
admin already has every field capability in the database (can_visit_stores,
can_file_report are true for admin), so this only tailors the experience:
a merchandiser view hides store visits and the report; a marketer view
shows both. The choice is a cookie, honoured only when the signed-in person
really is an admin, so it can never widen a field member's own access.

Exports: `ACTING_COOKIE`, `ActingRole`, `getActingRole`

## `src/lib/app-only.ts`

"Use the app" (migration 0084): an admin can require a merchandiser or
marketer to use the Xtend phone app. In a browser (or an installed web
page) they are sent to a page that tells them to download it, and signing
in from a browser is refused. Pure on purpose, so
scripts/check-app-only.ts can test it.

The apps put "XtendApp" in their user agent, and the middleware leaves the
xt_app cookie for the page loads Android's service worker makes without it
(src/lib/app-agent.ts). Anyone can send either, so this steers people to
the app; it is not a security control.

Exports: `APP_ONLY_ROLES`, `APP_ONLY_MESSAGE`, `APP_ONLY_CODE`, `APP_ONLY_PATH`, `appOnlyBlocks`

## `src/lib/app-update.ts`

Deciding what to tell someone about updates. Shared by the server
(/api/version) and the browser (UpdateManager); pure, so
scripts/check-updates.ts can exercise it.

Two kinds of update:
  - the site: every phone and browser runs the live site, so a new deploy
    only needs the page reloaded. A page knows its own build id
    (NEXT_PUBLIC_BUILD_ID) and compares it with the server's;
  - the phone app itself (the Android APK or the iPhone app), which needs
    installing. Only needed when something native changed, such as the
    shift tracker. An admin can set the lowest build still allowed.

Exports: `ReleaseNote`, `VersionInfo`, `UpdateLevel`, `UpdateState`, `buildNumber`, `decideUpdate`, `NOTES_FRESH_DAYS`, `shouldShowNotes`, `InstallStatus`, `installStatus`

## `src/lib/assistant-cache.ts`

What Ask Xtend may reuse instead of working out again, and for how long.
Pure on purpose (no server, no clock but the day passed in), so
scripts/check-assistant-cache.ts can test it.

Two things are reused, both only on the same server and only briefly:
  - a lookup the assistant already made (a day's attendance, a month's
    metrics): a past day cannot change, so it is kept for hours; anything
    that includes today is kept for a minute or two;
  - the whole answer to a question that was just asked the same way by the
    same person: five minutes, never when the turn proposed a change or a
    report (those are one-off cards) and never after a lookup failed.

## `src/lib/bot-guard.ts`

Xtend is a private staff app: nothing in it is for search engines, AI
crawlers, scrapers or scripts. The middleware asks `botDecision` about
every request it sees and answers 403 when the user agent is empty or
looks like one of those.

A user agent is easy to fake, so this only turns away the honest and
the lazy; the password check, the sign-in lockout (0077), the optional
human check (Turnstile) and the platform's firewall do the rest.

Never blocked, whatever they send:
- the scheduled jobs (`/api/cron/*`, which need CRON_SECRET; called by
  curl, `node run-job.mjs` and Vercel's cron);
- the phone's background tracker (`/api/track/*`, which needs its own
  token; old app builds send Java's or iOS's default user agent);
- health and version checks (`/api/health`, `/api/version`: Docker's
  HEALTHCHECK, deploy.sh, uptime monitors);
- static files and `robots.txt` (a crawler must be able to read it).

Exports: `OPEN_PATH_PREFIXES`, `OPEN_FILES`, `BOT_AGENT_PATTERNS`, `BotDecision`, `isOpenPath`, `isBotUserAgent`, `botDecision`, `BOT_BLOCKED_BODY`

## `src/lib/client-ip.ts`

The address a request came from, as the app's own proxy saw it.

X-Forwarded-For is a list each proxy appends to, so anything a client
writes in it comes first and the entries the proxies add come last. The
first entry is therefore whatever the caller chose to put there. This
reads from the end instead, skipping the proxies Xtend sits behind:

  TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=1  Nginx, Caddy or Traefik (Dokploy, Coolify) on the VPS, or Vercel (default)
  TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=2  Cloudflare in front of Nginx, and so on

Without the header (a request straight to Node), X-Real-IP, which Nginx
sets from the connection itself.

Exports: `requestIp`

## `src/lib/clock-notices.ts`

Telling someone that a clock-in or clock-out they made with no signal was
NOT recorded after all. Saved on the phone while offline, it is sent when
the signal returns; if the server then refuses it (for example the photo
had gone stale, or notifications were off), or it could not be sent in
time, the saved copy is deleted. Without a notice the person believes they
clocked in. The notice waits on this phone until Home shows it.

Pure on purpose (no browser APIs: the store is passed in), so
scripts/check-clock-notices.ts can test it.

Exports: `NoticeStore`, `CLOCK_NOTICES_KEY`, `clockNotice`, `addClockNotice`, `takeClockNotices`

src/lib/place-resolve.ts):

 1. Stores: the assigned outlet, then any store containing the spot.
 2. Places learned before (migration 024), and addresses Google gave
    before where there is no shop (0068). No API call.
 3. Google — Places (New) for the business name, Geocoding for the street
    address. This is the only source that reliably names Nigerian retail
    premises. Needs GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY with "Places API (New)" and
    "Geocoding API" enabled. Paid per request: answers are cached 30 days
    per spot, learned for good, counted per month (place_lookup_stats),
    and GOOGLE_MONTHLY_LOOKUP_LIMIT (20,000 when unset; 0 or none for no
    limit) stops Google for the rest of the month once reached.
 4. OpenStreetMap — Nominatim for the address, Overpass for a named
    business within 80 m. Free and needs no key, but Nigerian POI
    coverage is thin, so it often names the street rather than the shop.

Exports: `resolvePlace`, `placeForEvent`, `LocatedPlace`, `locateAddress`

## `src/lib/ip-geo.ts`

IP geolocation for the VPN / location-manipulation checks.

Free and keyless by default: ip-api.com returns a lat/lng, a country, and
crucially a proxy / hosting flag that marks VPN and datacentre IPs, with no
sign-up (45 requests a minute, which is far above Xtend's clock-in rate).
Swap the provider by pointing IP_GEO_URL at another HTTPS JSON endpoint that
uses the same field names, set IP_API_KEY to use ip-api's paid HTTPS
endpoint, or set IP_GEO_DISABLED=1 to turn the lookup off.

When the lookup cannot run (no network, a private IP, the rate limit), the
caller simply gets null and the IP-based checks are skipped for that event.
A clock-in is never blocked by this.

## `src/lib/place-resolve.ts`

The order in which Xtend names a spot, and the rule that keeps Google for
spots it has never seen. Pure: the providers are passed in, so the order
can be checked without a database or a network (scripts/check-places-usage.ts).
src/lib/geocode.ts supplies the real ones.

  1. the person's own store, when they stand inside its geofence;
  2. any store Xtend knows;
  3. a place Xtend learned before (named by a map or by staff);
  4. an address Google gave before for this spot (no shop there);
  5. Google, for the shop's name (its answers are also kept 30 days per
     spot in the server's cache), unless this is only a preview or this
     month's limit is used;
  6. OpenStreetMap, free.

`order: 'osm-first'` (PLACE_LOOKUP_ORDER=osm-first) asks OpenStreetMap
first and Google only when OpenStreetMap names no business: cheaper, with
fewer shop names.

What a map finds is learned, so the next lookup there stops at 3 or 4.

## `src/lib/storage-path.ts`

Whether a storage path a phone sent is a file in the caller's own folder.

`path.startsWith(uid + '/')` is not enough: storage does not tidy
`<uid>/../<someone-else>/x.jpg`, so a server-side (service role) read of
that path would fetch another person's photo. Only plain names are
accepted: `<uid>/<name>` or `<uid>/<folder>/<name>`, each part letters,
digits, dot, dash or underscore, never `.` or `..`, never empty.

Exports: `MAX_STORAGE_PATH`, `isOwnStoragePath`

## `src/lib/support-assistant.ts`

The AI that answers a field member's support message.

It reads the whole thread, replies in plain language to what it can handle
on its own (how the app works, what a status means, what to do next), and
when the issue needs a person, or it is not sure, it says so briefly and
escalates the thread to the office. It never changes an account, a store
allocation, a password or a record: those are exactly what it escalates.

Runs with the service-role client, because it writes the AI's reply and,
on escalation, pushes to the office. It is called from the support routes
after the member's message is saved.

Exports: `supportAssistantConfigured`, `respondToSupportThread`

## `src/lib/ttl-cache.ts`

A small in-memory cache for work that is the same for many people: the
answer to a question already asked, the global rows every phone reads, a
lookup for a past day. It keeps load off the database and the paid APIs.

It only ever saves work and never decides who may see what: callers put
whatever decides access (the asker, their role) into the key. It holds at
most `max` entries (oldest-used dropped first), forgets an entry after its
time is up, and never keeps a failure.

A cache made with `shared` also keeps its entries in Redis when
REDIS_URL is set, so every app container reuses one answer: memory first,
then Redis, then the real work. Only `fetch`, `store` and `remember` use
Redis; `get` and `set` stay in memory. Shared values must survive JSON.
Without Redis, or while it is down, a shared cache is a memory cache.

Exports: `TtlCache`, `namedCache`

## `src/lib/turnstile.ts`

Cloudflare Turnstile: an optional "are you human?" check on the sign-in

for the server); without them sign-in works exactly as before. The
widget runs in "managed" mode, so most people never see a puzzle.

Exports: `TURNSTILE_VERIFY_URL`, `TURNSTILE_SCRIPT_URL`, `TURNSTILE_ERROR`, `turnstileEnabled`, `turnstileSiteKey`, `TurnstileResult`, `parseSiteverify`, `verifyTurnstile`

Naming takes two live photos from the in-app camera, never from the
gallery: the store sign from outside, then a selfie holding one of our
products. The position saved is the phone's GPS fix, read by the app
when the first photo is taken. Next time anyone stands there, Xtend
recognises the place.

Exports: `PlaceDue`, `NamePlace`

## `src/components/field/use-dashboard-refresh.ts`

Keep the phone dashboard in step with the backend.

The fast path is Supabase realtime Broadcast: a database trigger sends one
lightweight event to the member's own private topic `field:<uid>` whenever
their attendance, store visit, support message or notification changes
(migration 0058). The event carries only { table, op }; the screen re-fetches
on it and that fetch goes through RLS, so the socket never carries row data.
Broadcast replaces Postgres Changes here because it does not run RLS per
subscriber per change, so the same Supabase compute holds far more
connections — the thing that caps how many staff can be on shift at once.

Behind it sits a slow poll as a safety net for anything realtime can miss:
a dropped socket, or a value the server computes only when the page is
read. It is far slower than the old 15s poll, because realtime now does the
work that used to need constant refreshing, which also makes the app feel
quicker and spares the battery and data.

At scale (thousands of field staff on shift at once) three things matter:
  - Only on-shift members hold a socket (see below); everyone else polls.
  - NEXT_PUBLIC_REALTIME_DISABLED=1 turns realtime off fleet-wide and lets
    everyone ride the poll instead — a safe release valve if the socket
    count is still the thing falling over.
  - If every client polled on the same 45s boundary the backend would see a
    spike every 45s instead of steady traffic, so the poll is jittered per
    client to spread that load out.

Exports: `useDashboardRefresh`

## `src/middleware.ts`

Refreshes the Supabase session cookie on every navigation so field staff
are not logged out mid-shift, and keeps unauthenticated users off the app.
Role enforcement itself lives in Postgres; this is only routing.

It must live in src/, beside app/: Next.js ignores a middleware file at
the project root when the app is under src/.

Exports: `middleware`, `config`

## `public/sw.js`

Xtend service worker.
Deliberately small. The app shell is cached so a cold start on 3G is not a
white screen, and navigations fall back to /offline when the network is
gone. Writes are NOT replayed here: they live in the IndexedDB outbox and
are flushed by the page, which owns the auth session.
